title: Peak load per window
prompt:
loads[i] is a server's load at second i; for every window of k consecutive seconds, report the peak load, returning the peaks in window order.

- loads has 1 to 100,000 integers between -10^4 and 10^4; 1 <= k <= len(loads).
- Return a list of len(loads) - k + 1 integers; entry i is max(loads[i : i + k]).
- Aim for O(n) time.
hints: Recomputing each window's max is O(n·k). Which values can never be a future maximum?
Once a larger value arrives, every earlier smaller value in the window is useless for all later windows too. Keep only candidates, in decreasing order.
Hold indices in a deque with decreasing loads: pop the back while it is <= the new load, push the new index, pop the front if it has left the window, and once r >= k - 1 the front is the peak.

solution.explanation: The deque keeps indices of the current window whose loads strictly decrease from front to back; anything no larger than a newer value is dropped because it can never be a peak again. The front is therefore the window maximum, and it is removed once it falls out of range. Each index is pushed and popped at most once.

complexity.notes: The deque holds at most k indices (excluding the output). A heap with lazy deletion gives O(n log n).

followUps: Return the window minimums as well in the same pass.
How would you report the peak of the last k readings on an unbounded stream with O(k) memory?
